claims.text: LLMs are systematically more confident when providing reasoning before answering multiple choice questions.
The increase in confidence due to reasoning is larger when the LLM's selected answer is incorrect than when it is correct.
Chain-of-Thought prompting degrades LLM calibration by increasing the proportion of high-confidence wrong answers.
Reasoning inflates confidence estimates because answer prediction depends jointly on the question and self-generated reasoning tokens.

evidence.description: Experiments on a general knowledge benchmark covering 57 subjects across seven LLMs demonstrated a systematic increase in response confidence under reasoning.
Comparative measurements of token probability increases on incorrect vs correct responses across 57 subjects.
Evaluation using standard metrics including Expected Calibration Error (ECE) and Brier score.

methodologies.name: CoT vs. Direct Answering MCQ Calibration Evaluation
methodologies.description: Evaluating confidence and probability calibration across direct and Chain-of-Thought answering modes using standard metrics.

limitations.text: LLM-estimated probabilities with CoT prompting are prone to inflated confidence and degraded calibration, making them unsafe for evaluation or metacognitive mechanisms.
